ICLR 2026

Retro*: Optimizing LLMs for Reasoning-Intensive Document Retrieval

Problem. Existing reasoning-enhanced IR approaches face challenges in applicability, scalability, and efficiency when retrieving documents with implicit or indirect relevance to tasks.
Approach. We propose Retro*, a rubric-based relevance scoring mechanism with test-time scaling via score integration of multiple reasoning trajectories, optimized with a novel reinforcement learning algorithm employing composite rewards.
Contribution. Retro* achieves state-of-the-art performance on the BRIGHT benchmark, outperforming existing document retrieval methods.
rubric-based scoringtest-time scalingreinforcement learningreasoning trajectories
ICLR 2026

Asymmetric Proximal Policy Optimization: mini-critics boost LLM reasoning

Problem. Standard reinforcement learning for LLMs relies on average advantage baselines, avoiding expensive value functions that often fail under sparse rewards and long reasoning horizons.
Approach. AsyPPO restores the critic role via a set of lightweight mini-critics trained on disjoint prompt shards, uses inter-critic uncertainty to refine policy updates by masking redundant advantages and filtering high-divergence states.
Contribution. Achieves >6% performance gains on Qwen3-4B-Base and ~3% on larger models compared to GRPO, improving learning stability.

SPG: Sandwiched Policy Gradient for Masked Diffusion Language Models

Problem. Reinforcement learning for diffusion LLMs is challenging because intractable log-likelihood prevents direct application of standard policy gradient methods.
Approach. SPG leverages both upper and lower bounds of true log-likelihood for more accurate policy gradient estimation compared to one-sided ELBO approximations.
Contribution. Significantly outperforms ELBO-based methods with accuracy improvements of 3.6% on GSM8K, 2.6% on MATH500, 18.4% on Countdown, and 27.0% on Sudoku.
sandwiched policy gradientdiffusion language modelsreinforcement learninglog-likelihood bounds

GAR: Generative Adversarial Reinforcement Learning for Formal Theorem Proving

Problem. Expensive online RL for theorem proving uses fixed problem sets, causing inefficient training and limiting capability on complex theorems.
Approach. GAR jointly trains problem composer and solver in adversarial loop with implicit curriculum learning that aligns task difficulty to prover capability.
Contribution. GAR achieves 4.20% relative improvement in pass@32 on MiniF2F-Test and improves DeepSeek-Prover-V2's ProofNet-Test pass@32 from 22.58% to 25.81%.
generative adversarial reinforcement learningcurriculum learningtheorem proving

LaSeR: Reinforcement Learning with Last-Token Self-Rewarding

Problem. Self-verification training for LLMs requires sequential generation of solutions and verifications, doubling inference cost.
Approach. LaSeR reveals that reasoning reward equals last-token self-rewarding score; augment RLVR loss with MSE loss aligning last-token scores with verifier rewards.
Contribution. Joint training of reasoning and self-rewarding provides auxiliary reward signals in both training and testing with reduced inference cost.
reinforcement learningself-rewardinglast-token prediction

RM-R1: Reward Modeling as Reasoning

Problem. Reward models lack interpretability and deep reasoning before assigning judgments, limiting alignment quality.
Approach. RM-R1 formulates reward modeling as reasoning task with chain-of-rubrics mechanism; train via distillation and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards.
Contribution. Outperforms larger open-weight (INF-ORM-Llama3.1-70B) and proprietary models (GPT-4o) by up to 4.9% on reward model benchmarks.

Look Back to Reason Forward: Revisitable Memory for Long-Context LLM Agents

Problem. LLMs struggle with long-context question answering when key evidence is dispersed across millions of tokens, especially with methods that process documents in a single forward pass.
Approach. ReMemR1 augments memory with callback-enhanced retrieval that allows selective access to the entire history and non-linear reasoning over early evidence, combined with Reinforcement Learning with Multi-Level Rewards (RLMLR) that provides both final-answer and step-level supervision.
Contribution. Experiments on long-document QA show significant gains over existing memory-based approaches, validating ReMemR1 as an effective solution for long-context reasoning agents.

Achieving Expert-Level Agent from Foundation Model via Complexity Curriculum Reinforcement Learning with Synthetic Data

Problem. LLM agents struggle with geometry problem solving due to weak heuristics for auxiliary constructions, and AI methods remain dominated by models relying heavily on large-scale data synthesis.
Approach. InternGeometry iteratively proposes and verifies propositions and auxiliary constructions using a symbolic engine and reflects on feedback with a dynamic memory mechanism enabling 200+ interactions per problem, trained with Complexity-Boosting Reinforcement Learning (CBRL).
Contribution. InternGeometry solves 44 of 50 IMO geometry problems (2000-2024), exceeding the average gold medalist score (40.9), using only 13K training examples, 0.004% of the data used by AlphaGeometry 2.

A$^2$FM: An Adaptive Agent Foundation Model for Tool-Aware Hybrid Reasoning

Problem. Reasoning-centric and agentic LLMs have fundamentally different strengths, causing inefficiency when reasoning models overthink or agentic models over-call tools on simple queries.
Approach. A2FM introduces route-then-align principle with three modes (reasoning, agentic, instant), where Adaptive Policy Optimization enforces adaptive sampling across modes with cost-regularized reward.
Contribution. On 32B scale achieves 13.4% on BrowseComp, 70.4% on AIME25, 16.7% on HLE, reducing cost per correct answer by 45.2% vs reasoning and 33.5% vs agentic.

Linking Process to Outcome: Conditional Reward Modeling for LLM Reasoning

Problem. Process Reward Models either treat reasoning steps in isolation or fail to align process rewards with final outcomes, causing ambiguous credit assignment and vulnerability to reward hacking.
Approach. Conditional Reward Modeling (CRM) conditions step rewards on preceding steps and explicitly links to final outcomes, enforcing conditional probability rules to capture causal relationships among reasoning steps.
Contribution. CRM consistently outperforms existing reward models across Best-of-N sampling, beam search, and RL, providing more reliable cross-sample comparison and robustness to reward hacking.

Approach. Introduces Visual Attention Score (VAS) metric to quantify visual token attention, reveals lazy attention localization phenomenon, and proposes AVAR framework with visual-anchored data synthesis and attention-guided objectives.
Contribution. AVAR delivers average gain of 7.0% across seven multimodal reasoning benchmarks when applied to Qwen2.5-VL-7B.

Problem. Open-source models struggle with large-scale, diverse-format data files and long-horizon multi-step reasoning required for real-world data analytics.
Approach. DataMind applies fine-grained task taxonomy, recursive task composition, knowledge-augmented sampling, and dynamically adjustable SFT+RL training on DataMind-12K, a high-quality trajectory dataset.

CDE: Curiosity-Driven Exploration for Efficient Reinforcement Learning in Large Language Models

Problem. RLVR methods often explore poorly leading to premature convergence and entropy collapse; policies are poorly calibrated and remain confident regardless of correctness.
Approach. CDE uses curiosity signals from actor (perplexity) and critic (value-estimate variance) as exploration bonuses within RLVR framework.
Contribution. Approximately +3 point improvement on AIME benchmarks; actor-wise bonus penalizes overconfident errors and critic-wise bonus connects to count-based exploration.

Problem. RLVR training on MLLMs leads to entropy collapse, policy degradation, or over-exploitation; uncontrolled exploration is inefficient.
Approach. CalibRL hybrid-policy framework with distribution-aware advantage weighting and asymmetric activation leveraging expert guidance for calibrated exploration.
Contribution. Maintains productive stochasticity while avoiding erroneous convergence; consistent improvements across eight in-domain and out-of-domain benchmarks.

When More is Less: Understanding Chain-of-Thought Length in LLMs

Problem. Longer Chain-of-Thought reasoning is assumed to always improve LLM performance, but this relationship is not well understood across models and tasks.
Approach. The paper demonstrates through controlled experiments that task accuracy follows an inverted U-shape with CoT length, with optimal length scaling with task difficulty and inversely with model capability.
Contribution. Error-accumulation analysis explains overthinking effects; training with optimally sized CoTs and length-aware filtering improves performance substantially.

Problem. Retrieval-augmented generation can be derailed by wrong or conflicting retrieved text, causing models to rely on inaccurate evidence.
Approach. Knowledgeable-R1 uses reinforcement learning to train models to exploit parametric knowledge when context is misleading, learning both local and global advantages with asymmetric transformation amplifying exploratory behaviors.

Problem. REINFORCE and GRPO are typically considered on-policy algorithms with limited off-policyness tolerance, limiting data reuse efficiency in LLM RL.
Approach. Provides first-principles derivation showing group-relative REINFORCE admits native off-policy interpretation without assuming training distribution.
Contribution. Demystifies GRPO myths and offers principles for off-policy adaptation via regularization and distribution shaping, validated through empirical studies.

Problem. Training reasoning capabilities in LLMs depends on human-curated problem-answer pairs and domain-specific reward engineering, limiting scalability.

Risk-Sensitive Reinforcement Learning for Alleviating Exploration Dilemmas in Large Language Models

Problem. Standard RL for LLMs struggles to escape local optima of pre-trained policies, boosting single-solution accuracy at the expense of solution diversity and multi-solution performance.
Approach. Adopt a risk-seeking objective interpolating between mean and maximum rewards, derive Risk-Sensitive GRPO that emphasizes hard prompts to drive exploration.
Contribution. RS-GRPO consistently improves pass@k performance across six mathematical reasoning benchmarks and five LLMs while enhancing or maintaining pass@1.

Problem. Self-training RL without gold labels relies on majority votes which may be spurious, hindering continual self-improvement on harder tasks.
Approach. Convert absence of gold labels into learning signal through self-penalization, penalizing overconfident rollouts and low-consistency examples while preserving promising chains.
Contribution. RESTRAIN achieves up to 140.7% pass@1 boost on AIME25 with only unlabeled data, nearly matching gold-label training on Qwen3-4B and OctoThinker-8B.

Soft Tokens, Hard Truths

Problem. Using continuous tokens during reasoning in LLMs is theoretically more expressive but has been limited by strong training difficulties and practical scalability challenges.
Approach. The paper introduces a scalable RL method to learn continuous CoTs using soft tokens (token mixtures with noise) without distilling from ground-truth discrete CoTs.
Contribution. Training with continuous CoTs matches discrete tokens on Pass@1 and surpasses them on Pass@32 across Llama and Qwen models up to 8B, demonstrating greater CoT diversity.

Count Counts: Motivating Exploration in LLM Reasoning with Count-based Intrinsic Rewards

Problem. Reinforcement learning for LLM reasoning relies on sparse outcome-based rewards and limited exploration, driving models toward repetitive and suboptimal patterns.
Approach. MERCI augments policy optimization with a principled intrinsic reward based on count-based exploration using a lightweight Coin Flipping Network to estimate pseudo counts and epistemic uncertainty.
Contribution. MERCI encourages richer and more varied chains of thought, significantly improves performance over strong baselines on complex reasoning benchmarks, and helps escape local routines.

Micro-Macro Retrieval: Reducing Long-Form Hallucination in Large Language Models

Problem. Large language models hallucinate facts in long-form generation because retrieved evidence is injected early in reasoning chains rather than staying close to the final outputs.
Approach. Micro-Macro Retrieval retrieves coarse-grained evidence at the macro level while extracting and reusing essential results from a key information repository at the micro level during generation, keeping critical facts near outputs.
Contribution. M^2R reduces hallucination in long-form tasks using curriculum learning-based RL with customized rewards, demonstrating effectiveness across multiple benchmarks especially in lengthy-context settings.

Beyond Binary Rewards: Training LMs to Reason About Their Uncertainty

Problem. RL training for reasoning improves accuracy but uses binary rewards that don't penalize guessing, degrading calibration and increasing hallucinations in other domains.
Approach. RLCR (Reinforcement Learning with Calibration Rewards) augments binary correctness with Brier score for confidence estimation, training models to generate both predictions and calibrated confidence.
Contribution. RLCR proves models with proper scoring rule rewards are both accurate and well-calibrated, substantially improving calibration in-domain and out-of-domain without accuracy loss.

Approach. TAMPO recasts temperature control as a learnable meta-policy updated via hierarchical two-loop process rewarding temperatures that maximize high-advantage trajectories.

Approach. DQO uses determinantal point processes to jointly optimize for quality and semantic diversity by measuring diversity as the volume spanned by response embeddings.

DELTA-Code: How RL Unlocks and Transfers New Programming Algorithms in LLMs

Problem. It remains unclear whether LLMs can acquire genuinely new reasoning strategies beyond skills encoded during pre-training, particularly for algorithmic coding tasks.
Approach. DELTA-Code is a controlled benchmark using templated problem generators to probe learnability (can RL solve problems with zero pretrained pass rate?) and transferrability (do learned skills generalize to OOD problems?).

Test-Time Alignment for Large Language Models via Textual Model Predictive Control

Problem. Test-time alignment of LLMs via guided decoding faces curse of horizon (token-level actions) or curse of dimensionality (response-level actions), creating fundamental trade-offs.
Approach. TMPC (Textual Model Predictive Control) inspired by control theory uses Hindsight Subgoal Identification to discover meaningful task-specific planning steps, then Subgoal-Conditioned Re-Generation for stable improvement.
Contribution. TMPC resolves the alignment trade-off by using retrospectively-identified subgoals to guide generation, achieving stable improvement on machine translation and code generation tasks.

Problem. Multi-turn tool-integrated reasoning with reinforcement learning suffers from training instability and degraded performance due to harmful negative samples from distributional drift and compounding external tool errors.

We add over 1700 low-resource languages to the data mix only during the decay phase, showing that it boosts performance dramatically and maximizes the gains from the relatively small amount of training data without excessive repetition. The model uses recent advances in architecture and training schemes to be faster and more multilingual than other models and we release weights, data, and code. ICML 2026

Sparser Block-Sparse Attention via Token Permutation

Problem. Scaling the context length of large language models (LLMs) offers significant benefits but is computationally expensive. This expense stems primarily from the self-attention mechanism, whose $O(N^2)$ complexity with respect to sequence length presents a major bottleneck for both memory and latency. Fortunately, the attention matrix is often sparse, particularly for long sequences, suggesting an opportunity for optimization. Block-sparse attention has emerged as a promising solution that partitions sequences into blocks and skips computation for a subset of these blocks. However, the effectiveness of this method is highly dependent on the underlying attention patterns, which can lead to sub-optimal block-level sparsity. For instance, important key tokens for queries within a single block may be scattered across numerous other blocks, leading to computational redundancy. In this work, we propose Permuted Block-Sparse Attention (**PBS-Attn**), a plug-and-play method that leverages the permutation properties of attention to increase block-level sparsity and enhance the computational efficiency of LLM prefilling. We conduct comprehensive experiments on challenging long-context datasets, demonstrating that PBS-Attn consistently outperforms existing block-sparse attention methods in model accuracy and closely matches the full attention baseline. Powered by our custom permuted-FlashAttention kernels, PBS-Attn achieves an end-to-end speedup of up to $\mathbf{2.75\times}$ in long-context prefilling, confirming its practical viability. Code available at \url{https://github.com/xinghao.
Approach. Proposes a method to address the problem.
Contribution. Scaling the context length of large language models (LLMs) offers significant benefits but is computationally expensive. We conduct comprehensive experiments on challenging long-context datasets, demonstrating that PBS-Attn consistently outperforms existing block-sparse attention methods in model accuracy and closely matches the full attention baseline. Powered by our custom permuted-FlashAttention kernels, PBS-Attn achieves an end-to-end speedup of up to $\mathbf{2.75\times}$ in long-context prefilling, confirming its practical viability. Empty Shelves or Lost Keys? Recall Is the Bottleneck for Parametric Factuality

Problem. Standard factuality evaluations of LLMs treat all errors alike, obscuring whether failures arise from missing knowledge (empty shelves) or from limited access to encoded facts (lost keys).
Approach. We propose a behavioral framework that profiles factual knowledge at the level of facts rather than questions, characterizing each fact by whether it is encoded, and then by how accessible it is: cannot be recalled, can be directly recalled, or can only be recalled with inference-time computation (thinking).
Contribution. To support such profiling, we introduce WikiProfile, a new benchmark constructed via an automated pipeline with a prompted LLM grounded in web search.

Problem. Large Language Models (LLMs) have rapidly advanced, with Gemini-3-Pro setting a new performance milestone.

Contribution. We first revisit LLM routing and aggregation at scale and identify three key bottlenecks: (1) current train-free routers are limited by a query-based paradigm focusing solely on textual similarity; (2) recent aggregation methods remain largely static, failing to select appropriate aggregators for different tasks; (3) the complementarity of routing and aggregation remains underutilized.
